claims.text: Claurst exposes /thinking to toggle extended thinking and /effort to set a level (low, medium, high, or max) for the session.
CLI flags --thinking <tokens> and --effort <level> set a token budget and effort level for the claurst binary.
The max effort level is only supported by models exposing it in the API (currently Opus 4.6 generation); unsupported models fall back to high.
Effort levels low, medium, and high persist to ~/.claude.json across sessions, while max and numeric token budgets are session-scoped.
The CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL environment variable overrides the persisted effort setting for the current process, with a warning shown on conflict with /effort.
Auto-compaction summarises conversation history when token usage crosses the effective context window minus a 13,000-token buffer, replacing messages with a compact summary.
Compaction can be controlled via DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1 (auto off, /compact manual), DISABLE_COMPACT=1 (fully off), and a CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE threshold override.
The /context command shows token usage relative to the context window, with warning/error thresholds 20,000 tokens before the limit and a blocking limit 3,000 tokens before it.
Sessions are stored as JSONL files under ~/.claurst/projects/<base64url(project-root)>/<session-id>.jsonl, with per-session metadata at ~/.claurst/sessions/<id>.json.
Session commands include /resume (alias /continue), /fork, /rename, /export, /rewind, and /session for remote sessions.
A public SDK exports getSessionMessages, listSessions, getSessionInfo, renameSession, tagSession, and forkSession for programmatic session access.
Plan mode restricts the model to read-only operations; write and execute operations require explicit permission, and ExitPlanModeTool returns to the normal permission model.
The goal system lets Claurst work autonomously across turns toward one objective, stopping on GoalCompleteTool with audit, /goal pause or clear, a 200-turn runaway guard, or token budget exhaustion.
Goal completion requires GoalCompleteTool with audit_summary and evidence arguments; calls without real evidence are rejected.
Managed agents provide a manager-executor architecture: the manager delegates subtasks to executor agents running in parallel up to a configurable concurrent limit, and does not execute tools itself.
Managed-agent budget split policies include shared, percentage (e.g. manager 20%), and fixed per-agent dollar caps, with a total budget set via /managed-agents budget.
The managed-agents API is documented as a preview feature under active development that may change in future releases.
Speech modes like /caveman and /rocky compress model responses (roughly 40-85% token reduction depending on variant), and /normal resets to the standard style.
Headless mode via claurst --print processes a prompt non-interactively and prints the final response to stdout, accepting piped stdin input.
Output formats include plain text (default), json (full message array), and stream-json (newline-delimited stream), with json and stream-json requiring --verbose.
Budget-control flags --max-budget-usd, --max-turns, and --max-tokens stop the run when limits are reached, exiting with a corresponding error message.
Each user gets a deterministic companion generated by hashing the user ID with a seeded Mulberry32 PRNG; only name and personality are persisted to ~/.claude.json after hatching.
Companion visual bones (species, rarity, stats, eyes, hat, shiny) are never stored and are always recomputed from hash(userId).
Voice mode (/voice) is an experimental toggle that transcribes microphone input via the Deepgram streaming STT API and submits it as a prompt.
The /vim command toggles vim-style modal keybindings (normal/insert/visual) for the input buffer; the setting persists unless enabled per-session with --vim.
Bridge mode keeps a WebSocket connection open for remote control via claude.ai, in either an in-process topology or a daemon bridge where the agent can be respawned.
Claurst loads instruction files hierarchically: managed /etc/claude-code files, then user ~/.claurst files, then AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md in each directory from root to the working directory.
Permission modes are default (prompt before dangerous/write operations), plan (read-only), autoAccept (accept all tool calls), and bypassPermissions (skips permission checks entirely).
Tools are classified into risk tiers (forbidden, dangerous, execute, write, readonly) that determine default permission behaviour, e.g. readonly tools are allowed automatically.
BashTool classifies command strings against known dangerous patterns (e.g. rm -rf, dd if=) for higher risk ratings, and a PermissionRequest hook can intercept any tool call.
Custom slash commands defined in .claude/settings.json under customCommands expand to prompts when invoked and appear alongside built-in commands in the / menu.
The --add-dir flag grants read access to additional directories outside the working directory, and multiple --add-dir flags can be combined.
The LspTool communicates with a Language Server Protocol server, supporting hover, definition, references, symbols, and diagnostics operations with a documented input schema.
LSP servers must be configured in settings.json (e.g. rust-analyzer for Rust); if none is configured for a file's language, the tool returns an informative error.

Claurst needs credentials to call the Anthropic API or another provider's API, checking --api-key, settings.json api_key, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then profile and legacy OAuth token files in priority order.
Subagents spawned via the Agent tool can operate in isolated git worktrees; EnterWorktreeTool and ExitWorktreeTool switch the agent's working directory in and out of a worktree.
WorktreeCreate and WorktreeRemove hook events allow substituting an external worktree manager, so worktrees can be Docker containers, VMs, or other directory-backed isolation.

summary: The evidence consists of product documentation (docs/advanced.md, docs/auth.md) describing Claurst's runtime features: effort/thinking controls, auto-compaction, session storage and SDK, plan mode, goal system, managed agents, speech modes, headless mode, permission tiers, LSP tool, worktree isolation, and credential resolution. All prior claims were verified as supported; the worktree feature is now backed by cited slices. Evidence coverage: 177 of 400 packet slices were shown to the model; the rest were withheld by the prompt budget.
